title: Dasakam 34 — Śrī Rāmāvatāram
description: The descent of Rama, his forest exile, and the opening events of the search for Sita.

canonical_sanskrit.method: Transcribed from the numbered Sanskrit stanzas on the cited page; exact supplied verse text retained, not normalized.

canonical_roman.method: Transcribed from the numbered English (IAST) page; exact supplied transliteration retained, not normalized.

stanzas.sanskrit: गीर्वाणैरर्थ्यमानो दशमुखनिधनं कोसलेऽष्वृष्यशृङ्गे पुत्रीयामिष्टिमिष्ट्वा ददुषि दशरथक्ष्माभृते पायसाग्र्यम् । तद्भुक्त्या तत्पुरन्ध्रीष्वपि तिसृषु समं जातगर्भासु जातो रामस्त्वं लक्ष्मणेन स्वयमथ भरतेनापि शत्रुघ्ननाम्ना ॥ ३४-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: gīrvāṇairarthyamāno daśamukhanidhanaṃ kosale’ṣvṛṣyaśṛṅge putrīyāmiṣṭimiṣṭvā daduṣi daśarathakṣmābhṛte pāyasāgryam | tadbhuktyā tatpurandhrīṣvapi tisṛṣu samaṃ jātagarbhāsu jāto rāmastvaṃ lakṣmaṇena svayamatha bharatenāpi śatrughnanāmnā || 34-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: King Dasaratha performed Puthrakameshti yagam with help of sage Rishyashringa. Bhagwan himself emerged with paayasam and asked Dasharatha to distribute it to his three wives & Bhagwan incarnated as Rama together with Lakshmana, Bharatha and Satrugana.

stanzas.sanskrit: कोदण्डी कौशिकस्य क्रतुवरमवितुं लक्ष्मणेनानुयातो यातोऽभूस्तातवाचा मुनिकथितमनुद्वन्द्वशान्ताध्वखेदः । नॄणां त्राणाय बाणैर्मुनिवचनबलात् ताटकां पाटयित्वा लब्ध्वाऽस्मादस्त्रजालं मुनिवनमगमो देव सिद्धाश्रमाख्यम् ॥ ३४-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: kodaṇḍī kauśikasya kratuvaramavituṃ lakṣmaṇenānuyāto yāto’bhūstātavācā munikathitamanudvandvaśāntādhvakhedaḥ | nṝṇāṃ trāṇāya bāṇairmunivacanabalāt tāṭakāṃ pāṭayitvā labdhvā’smādastrajālaṃ munivanamagamo deva siddhāśramākhyam || 34-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: At the instruction by father, Rama took his bow accompanied by Lakshmana, went with Sage Vishwamitra to protect his noble yajnya and reached Dhandaka forest. The Sage taught them two mantras Bala and Atibala which gives great health and prevented fatigue. Rama killed Taadakaa, a demoness who was troubling the sages from doing yajnyas.

stanzas.sanskrit: मारीचं द्रावयित्वा मखशिरसि शरैरन्यरक्षांसि निघ्नन् कल्यां कुर्वन्नहल्यां पथि पदरजसा प्राप्य वैदेहगेहम् । भिन्दानश्चान्द्रचूडं धनुरवनिसुतामिन्दिरामेव लब्ध्वा राज्यं प्रातिष्ठथास्त्वं त्रिभिरपि च समं भ्रातृवीरैः सदारैः ॥ ३४-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: mārīcaṃ drāvayitvā makhaśirasi śarairanyarakṣāṃsi nighnan kalyāṃ kurvannahalyāṃ pathi padarajasā prāpya vaidehageham | bhindānaścāndracūḍaṃ dhanuravanisutāmindirāmeva labdhvā rājyaṃ prātiṣṭhathāstvaṃ tribhirapi ca samaṃ bhrātṛvīraiḥ sadāraiḥ || 34-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Mareecha came to disturb the yajna in the very beginning itself. Rama chased him a but killed the other rakshashas. 
Rama liberated Ahalya from her curse and united her with her husband. 
Rama and Lakshmana reached King Janaka's palace & Rama broke Shiva danush and married Seetha, daughter of Mother Earth

stanzas.sanskrit: आरुन्धाने रुषान्धे भृगुकुलतिलके सङ्क्रमय्य स्वतेजो याते यातोऽस्ययोध्यां सुखमिह निवसन् कान्तया कान्तमूर्ते । शत्रुघ्नेनैकदाऽथो गतवति भरते मातुलस्याधिवासं तातारब्धोऽभिषेकस्तव किल विहतः केकयाधीशपुत्र्या ॥ ३४-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: ārundhāne ruṣāndhe bhṛgukulatilake saṅkramayya svatejo yāte yāto’syayodhyāṃ sukhamiha nivasan kāntayā kāntamūrte | śatrughnenaikadā’tho gatavati bharate mātulasyādhivāsaṃ tātārabdho’bhiṣekastava kila vihataḥ kekayādhīśaputryā || 34-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Parasurama, the foremost of Bhrigu vamsam confronted Rama, blinded with rage and was defeated. Parasurama handed over all his powers to Rama and went away. Rama reached Ayodhya with Seetha and lived there happily. 
One day, Bharatha left to his uncle's house along with Sathrugana. During that time, King Dasaratha planned for pattabhishekam of Rama, but the ceremony was stopped by step mother Kaikeyi.

stanzas.sanskrit: tातोक्त्या यातुकामो वनमनुजवधूसम्युतश्चापधारः पौरानारुध्य मार्गे गुहनिलयगतस्त्वं जटाचीरधारी । नावा सन्तीर्य गङ्गामधिपदवि पुनस्तं भरद्वाजमारान्नत्वा तद्वाक्यहेतोरतिसुखमवसश्चित्रकूटे गिरीन्द्रे ॥ ३४-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: tātoktyā yātukāmo vanamanujavadhūsamyutaścāpadhāraḥ paurānārudhya mārge guhanilayagatastvaṃ jaṭācīradhārī | nāvā santīrya gaṅgāmadhipadavi punastaṃ bharadvājamārā-nnatvā tadvākyahetoratisukhamavasaścitrakūṭe girīndre || 34-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
To keep up father's words, Rama taking his bows and arrows, left to exile along with Seetha and brother Lakshmana. The people of Ayodhya were filled with grief. 
Rama reached the residence of Guhan who ferried the three, across the river Ganges and they reached sage Bharadwaja. Under his guidance, Rama along with Seetha and Lakshmana, left to Chitrakootam and lived peacefully.

stanzas.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा पुत्रार्तिखिन्नं खलु भरतमुखात् स्वर्गयातं स्वतातं तप्तो दत्त्वाम्बु तस्मै निदधिथ भरते पादुकां मेदिनीं च । अत्रिं नत्वाऽथ गत्वा वनमतिविपुलं दण्डकं चण्डकायं हत्वा दैत्यं विराधं सुगतिमकलयश्चारु भोः शारभङ्गीम् ॥ ३४-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: śrutvā putrārtikhinnaṃ khalu bharatamukhāt svargayātaṃ svatātaṃ tapto dattvāmbu tasmai nidadhitha bharate pādukāṃ medinīṃ ca | atriṃ natvā’tha gatvā vanamativipulaṃ daṇḍakaṃ caṇḍakāyaṃ hatvā daityaṃ virādhaṃ sugatimakalayaścāru bhoḥ śārabhaṅgīm || 34-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Rama came to know that his father died due to separation from his beloved son Rama, through Bharatha, was grief stricken and performed Tarpana for him. 
Rama gave his paadukas to keep them with Bharatha and  take care of kingdom in Rama's absence. 
Rama reached Dandaka forest, killed asura Viraada gave salvation to Sage Sharabangee.

stanzas.sanskrit: नत्वाऽगस्त्यं समस्ताशरनिकरसपत्राकृतिं तापसेभ्यः प्रत्यश्रौषीः प्रियैषी तदनु च मुनिना वैष्णवे दिव्यचापे । ब्रह्मास्त्रे चापि दत्ते पथि पितृसुहृदं वीक्ष्य भूयो जटायुं मोदाद्गोदातटान्ते परिरमसि पुरा पञ्चवट्यां वधूट्या ॥ ३४-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: natvā’gastyaṃ samastāśaranikarasapatrākṛtiṃ tāpasebhyaḥ pratyaśrauṣīḥ priyaiṣī tadanu ca muninā vaiṣṇave divyacāpe | brahmāstre cāpi datte pathi pitṛsuhṛdaṃ vīkṣya bhūyo jaṭāyuṃ modādgodātaṭānte pariramasi purā pañcavaṭyāṃ vadhūṭyā || 34-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Rama left Chitrakootam after Bharatha left. He met Sage Agastya  who gave him divine bow of Vishnu, Brahmastra, and other missiles to protect the sages from Rakshashas. 
Rama then reached panchavati on the banks of River Godavari and stayed happily with Seetha.

stanzas.sanskrit: प्राप्तायाः शूर्पणख्या मदनचलधृतेरर्थनैर्निः सहात्मा तां सौमित्रौ विसृज्य प्रबलतमरुषा तेन निर्लूननासाम् । दृष्ट्वैनां रुष्टचित्तं खरमभिपतितं दूषणं च त्रिमूर्धं व्याहिंसीराशरानप्ययुतसमधिकांस्तत्क्षणादक्षतोष्मा ॥ ३४-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: prāptāyāḥ śūrpaṇakhyā madanacaladhṛterarthanairniḥ sahātmā tāṃ saumitrau visṛjya prabalatamaruṣā tena nirlūnanāsām | dṛṣṭvaināṃ ruṣṭacittaṃ kharamabhipatitaṃ duṣaṇaṃ ca trimūrdhaṃ vyāhiṃsīrāśarānapyayutasamadhikāṃstatkṣaṇādakṣatoṣmā || 34-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Shoorpanakha, demoness attracted by Rama's beauty tried to lure him. Annoyed Rama, sent her to Lakshmana, who cut her nose in anger. Seeing her plight, Khar Dhooshanan and Trishira came to fight and got killed. Rama killed more than ten thousand Raakshasas all at once with his bow.

stanzas.sanskrit: सोदर्याप्रोक्तवार्ताविवशदशमुखादिष्टमारीचमायासारङ्गं सारसाक्ष्या स्पृहितमनुगतः प्रावधीर्बाणघातम् । तन्मायाक्रन्दनिर्यापितभवदनुजां रावणस्तामहार्षीत्तेनार्तोऽपि त्वमन्तः किमपि मुदमधास्तद्वधोपायलाभात् ॥ ३४-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: sodaryāproktavārtāvivaśadaśamukhādiṣṭamārīcamāyā-sāraṅgaṃ sārasākṣyā spṛhitamanugataḥ prāvadhīrbāṇaghātam | tanmāyākrandaniryāpitabhavadanujāṃ rāvaṇastāmahārṣī-ttenārto’pi tvamantaḥ kimapi mudamadhāstadvadhopāyalābhāt || 34-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Shoorpanaka went back to Ravana to tell about Seetha's beauty. Ravana got infatuated and devised plan to abduct her with help of Mareecha. Mareecha acting like a golden deer, lured Seetha and ran away. Rama went in search of it killed it but Mareecha shouted Lakshmana in Ram's voice before it died. Sensing danger, Lakshmana was forced to look for Rama by Seetha. When Seetha was alone, Ravana abducted her. Though Rama was very sad about his separation from Seetha, yet he was happy that now he got a reason for Ravana Vadham.

stanzas.sanskrit: भूयस्तन्वीं विचिन्वन्नहृत दशमुखस्त्वद्वधूं मद्वधेनेत्युक्त्वा याते जटायौ दिवमथ सुहृदः प्रातनोः प्रेतकार्यम् । गृह्णानं तं कबन्धं जघनिथ शबरीं प्रेक्ष्य पम्पातटे त्वं सम्प्राप्तो वातसूनुं भृशमुदितमनाः पाहि वातालयेश ॥ ३४-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman: bhūyastanvīṃ vicinvannahṛta daśamukhastvadvadhūṃ madvadhene-tyuktvā yāte jaṭāyau divamatha suhṛdaḥ prātanoḥ pretakāryam | gṛhṇānaṃ taṃ kabandhaṃ jaghanitha śabarīṃ prekṣya pampātaṭe tvaṃ samprāpto vātasūnuṃ bhṛśamuditamanāḥ pāhi vātālayeśa || 34-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Ravana caused fatal wounds to Jataayu for having tried to protect Seetha. While searching for Seetha, Rama found wounded Jataayu. Rama performed funeral rites for Jataayu and set on a searching mission with Lakshmana. 
A monster Kabandha obstructed their way and got killed by Rama. He granted salvation to pious Shabari and met Hanuman on the banks of River Pampaa.
